thread.title: Spotify: As Its IPO Nears, Here's the Competition

title: Spotify: As Its IPO Nears, Here's the Competition
text:
Large Photo: Getty Images 
Streaming music service provider Spotify is scheduled to begin trading on Tuesday ( with the ticker “SPOT” ) and the company is poised to build a long-term leadership position , according to a Thursday note from MKM Partners. 
Here’s what MKM thinks of possible challenges from Amazon (AMZN), Apple (AAPL), Facebook (FB), Alphabet-owned Google (GOOGL) and Pandora (P)—all of which are Barron’s Next 50 companies: 
• Amazon: It might actually help Spotify, since its service is likely to be important to the company’s digital assistant app library. Meanwhile, MKM wrote, “through the many iterations of its music platforms over the years, we have yet to be impressed by a compelling service offering.…We expect Amazon will maintain a music offering as part of a Prime member benefit, but we do not expect the service will become a major share player and challenge Spotify.” 
• Apple: The company has benefited from a “an older generation of die-hards” who’ve invested heavily in iTunes downloads, which is a shrinking market—but which may be hard to grow: “Apple has a captive audience from those die-hards invested in the platform and accustomed to the iTunes interface,” MKM wrote. “This is not an insignificant number, but we think share ultimately lands at levels less than the company’s iPhone market share which is about 20%.” 
• Facebook: The company’s moves to sign deals with major labels don’t necessarily presage a salvo against Spotify, according to MKM. “We view this more as Facebook sewing up potential holes on copyright infringement by users and not an indication the company is targeting a more aggressive push into digital music,” they wrote. “We think Facebook is an incredibly powerful platform for user acquisition, will benefit from the growth in digital music as a funnel for the contenders, and would not be surprised to see deeper collaboration with Spotify in the future.” 
• Google: This one, the analysts wrote, might be the biggest threat to Spotify. (We wrote about YouTube and music in December.) “Music is a very significant portion of overall consumption on YouTube and has been for many years,” MKM wrote. “The company has a massive amount of data, content that cannot be found on any other platform and we think the parent company is unparalleled in A.I. technology and ability to invest.” 
• Pandora: The opportunity to become a “major scale player,” MKM wrote, “has passed,” though it could still find a profitable niche: “The technology spending requirement to compete with Spotify is significantly beyond the company’s reach in our view. Pandora may be able to retain and potentially grow its U.S. base on strong secular trends away from broadcast radio, but we think it’s unlikely it will improve its relative position versus Spotify.” 
• MKM started coverage of Spotify with a $200 price target and a “buy” rating.
